solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild, like a kangaroo?

definitions.meaning: furiously angry, beside oneself with rage
a kangaroo moves by bounding, so whimsically it is mad on bounding along

explanation.surface: A comparison between a wild creature and an Australian marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wild with fury is in an idiomatic state of hopping rage; the second sense reads the phrase literally as bounding about.

clue.text: Trying to escape joining in a marathon?

definitions.meaning: taking part in a long race, literally out jogging

explanation.surface: Someone escaping by slipping in among marathon runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is idiomatically said to be fleeing in this phrase; a marathon participant is literally out jogging.

clue.text: Hurt as I dropped vessel

indicators.note: I is dropped, so the letter is taken out of the word for hurt

parts.note: hurt as a noun is pain

explanation.surface: Someone injured as they dropped a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a cooking vessel, a container for holding food on the stove.

clue.text: Improved new freezer

parts.note: an icer is something that ices or freezes

explanation.surface: An advert boasting of an upgraded new freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improved is better or more pleasant, a comparative of pleasant.

clue.text: Effete type weaving silk into unruly hair

indicators.note: into tells us the rearranged letters go inside the hair

parts.note: a mop is a thick untidy head of hair

indicators.note: weaving works the letters of silk into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A dandy plaits silk ribbons into his messy hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'unruly' describe the hair's state, but the whole phrase 'unruly hair' is one piece; 'weaving' alone stirs the fabric word.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, unmanly person, a weakling lacking spirit.

clue.text: Confuse with combination of noise and dirt

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are combined and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Noise and dirt together leave a person bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of' mixes the letters of NOISE and DIRT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorient someone is to bewilder them, making them lose their bearings.

clue.text: Sunscreen and singlet I put on

indicators.note: I is put on, added after the garment word

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless top

explanation.surface: Getting dressed for the sun: lotion and a vest on.
explanation.walkthrough: A topi (or topee) is a pith sun helmet worn in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun helmet shields the head from the sun, so it is a screen against sun.

clue.text: Hard worker on heroin a danger on computer

indicators.note: in a down clue, the worker sits on top of the drug word

parts.note: to work like a Trojan is to toil tirelessly
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug-using diligent employee poses a risk at the office computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious program disguised as useful software is a classic computer threat, named after the wooden horse of Troy.

clue.text: Under pressure, let out imploring word

indicators.note: in a down clue the renting word sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to lease property is to let it out

explanation.surface: Someone under stress blurts out a begging word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the polite word used when begging or asking for something.

clue.text: Proper to fix name of race

indicators.note: the abbreviation is fixed into the middle of the word for proper

parts.note: proper conduct is ethical

explanation.surface: A proper way to fix the name of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns ethnic groups, so it means relating to race.

clue.text: For unruly lot, hard to get into subject of parable

indicators.note: hard's letter gets into the parable figure

parts.note: the Parable of the Sower is one of Jesus's parables
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A preacher finds a parable hard to put across to an unruly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is British slang for a useless or disreputable bunch of people.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a shower is a contemptible or badly behaved crowd.

clue.text: Olympic sportsman who joins panels?

definitions.meaning: a competitor in the sword sport of the Olympics
someone building a garden boundary from panels

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete who sits on judging panels.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman in Olympic fencing, and whimsically a person erecting fence panels.

clue.text: Bright guy means to lift in a couple of hundred pieces of fuel

indicators.note: in puts the lifting device inside the hundreds

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two make CC
a lever is a means of lifting heavy things
logs are pieces of fuel for a fire

explanation.surface: A smart man works out how to lift hundreds of pieces of firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all or show-off with brains is derisively called this in British idiom.

clue.text: A grass mutates like this into a weed

indicators.note: mutates means changes form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A grass species mutates, turning into a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a floating brown seaweed, gulfweed, that gives the Sargasso Sea its name.

clue.text: Posh accent that gets Parliament going!

definitions.meaning: the received upper-class way of talking, as royalty does
the monarch's address that opens each session of Parliament

explanation.surface: A plummy voice that rouses Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A plummy royal way of talking, and the monarch's address at the State Opening that sets out the government's programme.

clue.text: Start blazing row, full of feminine emotion

indicators.note: the row word is full of the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or row
ire is anger, an emotion

explanation.surface: A furious row starts, full of a woman's emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to start it burning, so it means start blazing.

clue.text: One with a tale to tell finished interrupting queen

definitions.text: One with a tale to tell

indicators.note: the word for finished breaks into the queen's name

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the last queen of Henry VIII
done means finished

explanation.surface: Someone who has finished their story butts in on a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pardoner is a pilgrim who tells a tale in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Pardoner is one of the Canterbury pilgrims who each tell a tale.

clue.text: One no longer keen on farm machinery that does away with steam

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, one no longer in that role
an enthusiast for tractors

explanation.surface: A former enthusiast of tractors, now uninterested.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lapsed farm hobbyist; split as EX + TRACTOR FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen ventilator draws out steam and smells, removing them from the room.

clue.text: Very poor baby, small, uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of the words are removed, leaving the interior

explanation.surface: A tiny baby, left uncovered, in a dreadful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the first letter of baby and the last of small.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly bad, extremely poor in quality.

clue.text: Chap grabs glass that girl's left: I'm not sure there's much wine in it

indicators.note: the man grabs the remaining letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: the girl is left, gone from the word glass, leaving its first letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
um is a hesitant sound of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A man takes a glass a girl left behind, doubtful there's much wine in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is ironic: the hesitant 'I'm not sure' leads to a bottle holding a great deal of wine, twice a standard bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large bottle holding twice the standard amount of wine.

clue.text: Girl, cold, losing pounds in odd places

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name

indicators.note: the cold word loses one pound letter

parts.note: chilly means cold
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A girl with a cold slims down in odd spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchily means unevenly, here and there, occurring in scattered spots.

clue.text: Sailor comprehending what ocean is, turning dial

indicators.note: turning means the whole is read backwards
comprehending means containing, so the sailor holds the ocean word

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman, a sailor
the ocean is deep

explanation.surface: A sailor grasps the ocean's nature while turning a dial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' applies to the whole assembly, the sailor with the ocean word inside, not just to the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedo, short for speedometer, is the dial showing a vehicle's speed.

clue.text: Confess about part finally in police operation

indicators.note: the confession word goes about the last letter

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of part

explanation.surface: A suspect confesses their part in a police operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is an undercover police operation designed to trap criminals.

clue.text: Drop off tin with leak

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
to ooze is to leak slowly

explanation.surface: Dropping off a can that has a leak.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep briefly, a nap or doze.

clue.text: Back in the morning, queuing at this station?

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AM means in the morning
people queuing are in line

explanation.surface: Commuters return in the morning to queue at a big railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainline station is a major railway terminus on a principal route.

clue.text: Random allocation of large amount

explanation.definitionFit: Casting lots allocates things by chance; a large quantity is also called this.

clue.text: A very short book

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: most means very, as in most kind

explanation.surface: A really brief book.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Unavoidable shortly to do favour for a politician

indicators.note: shortly means the verb is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to oblige is to do someone a favour
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Doing a favour for a politician is inescapable.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligatory things are compulsory and so cannot be avoided.
